title: Reachability through an in-range length query
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $l,l_1,l_0$ machine labels, $st$ a seven-register state, and $c$ an abstract machine configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$ queries whether the whole input length exceeds the pointer register, with $l_1$ the positive-answer label and $l_0$ the negative-answer label. If every register of $st$ is at most $B$, the pointer value in $st$ is less than $|x|$, and there is a run from label $l_1$ with register values given by $st$ to $c$, with the guard satisfied at every earlier step, then there is such a guarded run from label $l$ with the same register values to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ is a whole-input query to the input-length decider using the pointer register, with branches $l_1$ and $l_0$
Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
The pointer value in $st$ is less than $|x|$
There is a guarded run from $(l_1,st)$ to $c$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $l,l_1,l_0$ control states, $st$ a
seven-register state, and $c$ a machine configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$
calls the input-length decider on the whole input, with the pointer register as its sole
argument, and branches to $l_1$ on a positive answer and $l_0$ on a negative answer. If
each register of $st$ is at most $B$, the pointer value is less than the length of $x$,
and there is a run from control state $l_1$ with register values given by $st$ to $c$
that satisfies the guard at every earlier step, then there is such a guarded run from
control state $l$ with the same register values to $c$.
